public.title: Rich Text to HTML
public.description: input {text,ranges}; text has at most 100 ASCII characters. Each range is [start,end,style] with half-open endpoints and style b or i. Styles combine by union. For each maximal run with equal active style set, emit escaped text wrapped in b then i (b outermost); unstyled text has no wrapper. Escape ampersand, less/greater signs, double/single quotes. Zero-length ranges have no effect. Adjacent equal style sets must merge. Return the canonical HTML string. Supported inputs are valid for this contract. Aggregate JSON-serialized input is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, nesting depth at most 6, arrays at most 40 items, operation/call lists at most 20 items, and individual strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless a tighter bound is stated. Integers have absolute value at most 1000; output arithmetic stays within safe integers. String object keys and string path segments are nonempty safe alphanumeric/underscore names excluding __proto__, constructor and prototype. Empty arrays/objects are allowed where consistent with the contract. Output ordering follows the rules above. These bounds include all nested payloads and all operations together.
hints: Separate the documented JSON representation from the behavior being modeled.
Preserve ordering and distinguish missing values, null, zero and false carefully.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, fixtures and reference solutions, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party exercise text or implementation copied.

explanation: Compute active styles per character, coalesce equal runs and wrap with canonical nesting. O(text length times range count plus output) time and O(text length plus output) space. Functional tests check the documented adapter behavior; they do not enforce implementation technique or prohibit built-in APIs.
